title: Array
definition: A contiguous block of memory storing elements of the same type. It supports O(1) random access based on index.

title: Linked List
definition: A linear collection of nodes where each node points to the next. It supports efficient insertions and deletions.

title: Singly Linked List
definition: A linked list where each node contains data and a pointer to the next node. Traversal is one-directional.

title: Doubly Linked List
definition: A linked list where each node has pointers to both previous and next nodes. It enables bidirectional traversal.

title: Circular Linked List
definition: A linked list in which the last node points back to the head. It forms a cycle for continuous traversal.

title: Stack
definition: A linear data structure that follows the LIFO principle. Push adds to the top; pop removes from the top.

title: Queue
definition: A linear data structure that follows the FIFO principle. Enqueue adds at the rear; dequeue removes from the front.

title: Deque
definition: A double-ended queue allowing insertion and deletion at both ends. It generalizes stacks and queues.

title: Priority Queue
definition: An abstract structure that serves elements by priority rather than insertion order. Heaps are common implementations.

title: Heap
definition: A complete binary tree that satisfies the heap property. It supports efficient find-min or find-max operations.

title: Min-Heap
definition: A heap where each node is less than or equal to its children. The minimum element is at the root.

title: Max-Heap
definition: A heap where each node is greater than or equal to its children. The maximum element is at the root.

title: Binary Search Tree
definition: A binary tree where left subtree keys are smaller and right subtree keys are larger. In-order traversal yields sorted order.

title: AVL Tree
definition: A self-balancing BST maintaining height balance factors. Rotations keep operations logarithmic.

title: Red-Black Tree
definition: A self-balancing BST using node colors and invariants. It guarantees O(log n) operations.

title: Splay Tree
definition: A self-adjusting BST that moves accessed nodes to the root. Amortized operations are logarithmic.

title: B-Tree
definition: A balanced search tree optimized for disks. Nodes can have many keys and children.

title: B+ Tree
definition: A variant of B-Tree where all data is stored in leaves. Internal nodes hold only keys for routing.

title: Trie
definition: A prefix tree for strings where edges represent characters. It enables efficient prefix queries.

title: Suffix Array
definition: An array of starting indices of all suffixes of a string sorted lexicographically. It supports fast pattern queries with LCP.

title: Suffix Tree
definition: A compressed trie of all suffixes of a string. It answers many string queries in linear time.

title: Hash Table
definition: A structure mapping keys to values using a hash function. Average-case operations are O(1).

title: Hashing with Chaining
definition: A collision resolution method storing colliding keys in buckets. Each bucket holds a list of entries.

title: Open Addressing
definition: A collision resolution method that probes alternative slots. Common variants are linear and quadratic probing.

title: Bloom Filter
definition: A probabilistic structure for set membership with false positives. It uses multiple hash functions over a bit array.

title: Graph
definition: A set of vertices connected by edges. It models relationships such as networks and dependencies.

title: Adjacency List
definition: A graph representation storing a list of neighbors for each vertex. It is memory-efficient for sparse graphs.

title: Adjacency Matrix
definition: A graph representation using a 2D matrix of edge presence. It is efficient for dense graphs.

title: Breadth-First Search
definition: A graph traversal exploring neighbors level by level. It finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

title: Depth-First Search
definition: A graph traversal exploring as far as possible along each branch. It is useful for cycle detection and components.

title: Topological Sort
definition: An ordering of DAG vertices where edges go from earlier to later. It exists only for acyclic directed graphs.

title: Kahn's Algorithm
definition: A topological sort method using in-degree and a queue. It removes zero in-degree nodes iteratively.

title: Tarjan's SCC
definition: An algorithm to find strongly connected components using DFS and low-link values. It runs in linear time.

title: Kosaraju's SCC
definition: An algorithm finding SCCs via two DFS passes. It uses graph reversal and finishing times.

title: Dijkstra's Algorithm
definition: A shortest-path algorithm for non-negative edge weights. It uses a priority queue to relax edges.

title: Bellman-Ford
definition: A shortest-path algorithm allowing negative weights. It detects negative cycles.

title: Floyd-Warshall
definition: An all-pairs shortest paths algorithm using dynamic programming. It runs in O(n^3) time.

title: Prim's Algorithm
definition: A greedy algorithm building a minimum spanning tree. It grows a tree from a starting vertex.

title: Kruskal's Algorithm
definition: A greedy algorithm selecting edges by increasing weight. It uses union-find to avoid cycles.

title: Union-Find
definition: A disjoint set data structure supporting union and find. Path compression and rank make it efficient.

title: Greedy Strategy
definition: An algorithmic paradigm making locally optimal choices. It often yields optimal solutions for matroids or MSTs.

title: Divide and Conquer
definition: A paradigm splitting problems into subproblems, solving recursively, and merging results.

title: Dynamic Programming
definition: An optimization technique storing solutions to subproblems. It converts exponential recursion to polynomial time.

title: Memoization
definition: A top-down dynamic programming technique caching recursive results. It avoids recomputing overlapping subproblems.

title: Tabulation
definition: A bottom-up dynamic programming technique filling tables iteratively. It often improves constant factors.

title: Backtracking
definition: A search strategy exploring candidates and undoing choices. It prunes branches that violate constraints.

title: Two Pointers
definition: A technique using two moving indices to narrow ranges. It solves problems on arrays and strings efficiently.

title: Sliding Window
definition: A technique maintaining a moving subarray to track counts or sums. It yields linear-time solutions on sequences.

title: Bit Manipulation
definition: Using bitwise operations to optimize computations. It encodes sets, states, and arithmetic tricks.

title: Quicksort
definition: A divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm using partition around a pivot. Average time is O(n log n).

title: Mergesort
definition: A stable divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm that merges sorted halves. It guarantees O(n log n) time.

title: Heapsort
definition: A comparison sort building a heap to repeatedly extract extremes. It runs in O(n log n) time.

title: Insertion Sort
definition: A simple stable sort building the result one item at a time. It is efficient on nearly sorted data.

title: Selection Sort
definition: A simple in-place sort repeatedly selecting the minimum. It performs O(n^2) comparisons.

title: Counting Sort
definition: A non-comparison sort counting occurrences of keys. It runs in O(n + k) time for small key ranges.

title: Radix Sort
definition: A non-comparison sort processing digits from LSD or MSD. It relies on stable intermediate sorts.

title: Bucket Sort
definition: A distribution sort grouping elements into buckets. Sorting each bucket yields near-linear expected time.

title: Shell Sort
definition: An in-place sort using diminishing gap insertion sorts. It improves over insertion sort on large arrays.

title: Stable Sorting
definition: Sorting that preserves the relative order of equal keys. It matters when keys contain multiple fields.

title: In-Place Algorithm
definition: An algorithm using only O(1) extra memory. It modifies input structures directly.

title: Time Complexity
definition: A measure describing how runtime grows with input size. Big-O provides an upper bound.

title: Space Complexity
definition: A measure describing additional memory usage versus input size. It includes auxiliary structures.

title: Big-O Notation
definition: An upper bound describing asymptotic growth. It hides constant factors and lower-order terms.

title: Big-Theta Notation
definition: A tight bound describing both upper and lower asymptotic growth. It captures exact order.

title: Big-Omega Notation
definition: A lower bound on asymptotic growth. It states that an algorithm runs at least this fast.

title: Amortized Analysis
definition: A technique averaging the cost of operations over sequences. It explains dynamic array resizing and union-find.

title: Recursion
definition: A technique where a function calls itself on smaller inputs. It requires base cases to terminate.

title: Recursion Tree Method
definition: A visualization for solving recurrences by expanding calls. It estimates total work by level.

title: Master Theorem
definition: A formula giving asymptotic bounds for common divide-and-conquer recurrences.

title: Hash Map vs Set
definition: A comparison between key-value and key-only hash structures. They differ by stored payload and operations.

title: LRU Cache
definition: A cache eviction policy removing the least recently used item. It is often implemented with a list and hash map.

title: LFU Cache
definition: A cache eviction policy removing the least frequently used item. It balances frequency and recency.

title: Skip List
definition: A probabilistic layered list supporting logarithmic searches. It trades randomness for balance.

title: Treap
definition: A randomized BST ordering nodes by key and heap priority. Rotations maintain heap and BST properties.

title: KD-Tree
definition: A space-partitioning tree for k-dimensional points. It accelerates nearest-neighbor queries.

title: Quadtree
definition: A tree partitioning 2D space into quadrants recursively. It supports spatial indexing and graphics.

title: Octree
definition: A tree partitioning 3D space into eight octants recursively. It is used in 3D graphics and collision detection.

title: Convex Hull
definition: The smallest convex polygon enclosing a set of points. Graham scan and Andrew's algorithm compute it.

title: KMP Algorithm
definition: A linear-time string matching algorithm using prefix function. It avoids re-checking matched prefixes.

title: Rabin-Karp
definition: A string matching algorithm using rolling hash for pattern search. It is efficient for multiple patterns.

title: Z Algorithm
definition: A linear-time string algorithm computing Z-values. It accelerates pattern matching and string processing.

title: Boyer-Moore
definition: A string search algorithm using bad-character and good-suffix heuristics. It skips large portions of text.

title: String Hashing
definition: Assigning numeric hashes to strings for fast comparison. Rolling hashes enable sliding window checks.

title: Manacher's Algorithm
definition: A linear-time algorithm to find longest palindromic substring using symmetry.

title: Edit Distance
definition: The minimum number of edits to transform one string into another. Levenshtein distance counts insertions, deletions, and substitutions.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
definition: A sequence problem finding a longest strictly increasing subsequence. Binary search yields O(n log n).

title: 0-1 Knapsack
definition: A DP optimization selecting items to maximize value under a weight budget. Each item can be taken once.

title: Unbounded Knapsack
definition: A DP variant where items can be taken unlimited times. It changes transition and complexity.

title: Coin Change
definition: A DP problem asking for the number or minimum coins to make a sum. It illustrates overlapping subproblems.

title: Matrix Exponentiation
definition: A technique raising matrices to powers to speed up linear recurrences. Fast exponentiation reduces complexity.

title: Fast Power
definition: Exponentiation by squaring to compute a^n quickly. It reduces multiplications logarithmically.

title: Fast Fourier Transform
definition: An algorithm to compute the discrete Fourier transform efficiently. It enables convolution and large integer multiplication.

title: Greatest Common Divisor
definition: The largest integer dividing two numbers without remainder. The Euclidean algorithm computes it efficiently.

title: Least Common Multiple
definition: The smallest positive integer that is a multiple of two numbers. It relates to GCD via lcm(a,b)=a*b/gcd(a,b).

title: Sieve of Eratosthenes
definition: A classic algorithm marking composite numbers to list primes up to n in O(n log log n).

title: Modular Arithmetic
definition: Arithmetic where numbers wrap around a modulus. It underpins hashing and cryptography.

title: Modular Inverse
definition: An integer x such that a·x ≡ 1 (mod m) when gcd(a,m)=1. It is central to division under modulo.

title: Chinese Remainder Theorem
definition: A theorem reconstructing numbers from residues modulo coprime moduli. It enables parallel modular computations.

title: Combinatorics nCr
definition: Counting the number of ways to choose r items from n. It uses factorials and modular inverses for large n.

title: Quickselect
definition: A selection algorithm finding the k-th smallest element. It uses partitioning like quicksort with average O(n) time.
